title: First Object to Use Subsurface Scattering Appearing in Scene Causes a Big Stutter
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproduceable in: v4.4.stable.steam [4c311cbee]

### System information

Windows 11 (build 26100) - Vulkan (Forward+) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6636) - AMD Ryzen 9 5900X 12-Core Processor (24 threads)

### Issue description

I think this problem may have also existed in prior 4.x builds of Godot, but I'm not knowledgeable enough about the internals to properly differentiate out this problem versus shader caching/compiling. All I know is a particular shader load in my main project which was previously taking about 0.25 seconds in Godot 4.3 is now sometimes taking a FULL SECOND in Godot 4.4.

Basically, upon starting a Godot program, the first time any object in the world is rendered on-screen with subsurface scattering enabled there's a BIG stutter, after which everything works as intended. I thought this might be a caching issue at first and maybe it is, but I have noted that if multiple different materials are using subsurface scattering only the first one to render on-screen will cause a giant stutter, while any subsequent such materials don't stutter at all.

The size of the stutter is not consistent either. Occasionally it's only a tiny fraction of a second, sometimes it's OVER a second. The size of the stutter seems to be related to GPU caching because the more work I do in the Godot editor before hitting this problem again, the larger the stutter tends to be.

Obviously a workaround is to just load in shaders on a loading screen the same as one previously would before Ubershaders, but I wanted to draw attention to this because it sounds like this should've been addressed by the Ubershader system in the first place.

### Steps to reproduce

Simply run a project where no objects are rendered at first using subsurface scattering, then have such an object with subsurface scattering come into view. There will ALWAYS be a stutter when this first occurs, but no stutters will occur following.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mrp_for_subsurface_scattering_bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19063041/mrp_for_subsurface_scattering_bug.zip)

When run, this minimal reproduction project shows a spinning capsule in the background. After a few seconds the capsule will stutter just as a torus with subsurface scattering enters from the left side. A little later another torus with a different material using subsurface scattering will enter but this one won't cause a stutter. The stutter will likely be less noticeable (but still present) the more times in a row you run the project.
